## nlmixr2llm · estimation {#nlmixr2llm-estimation}

[nlmixr2/nlmixr2llm at `50f236a`](https://github.com/nlmixr2/nlmixr2llm/tree/50f236acea6de31ced5780abbb4c27a26c2f88cc/inst/skills/estimation) · tool skill · rank 3 · tags: nlmixr2; estimation

| S | Q | E | M | U |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 27.8 | 21.4 | 13.0 | 88.8 | 30.0 |

**Quality.** 5 of 7 applicable rubric items met (71.4), less 2 major and 0 minor errors.

| Item | | Evidence |
|:---|:---|:---|
| R1 States what the skill does not do | ✅ yes | "`nonmem`, `monolix`, `pknca`, `nlmer`, `saemix` \| babelmixr2 — see the `interop` skill." (SKILL.md methods table) hands those backends to another skill. |
| R2 Cites sources for its recommendations | no | 4 of 10 sampled recommendations name a source (AgentODE, censoring vignette, nlmixr2nn vignette and issue); the log scale, the 3.84 drop in OFV and the shrinkage cut-off cite none. |
| R6 States the limitations of its own output | ✅ yes | "Report estimates with their precision and any caveats (shrinkage, bounds, non-convergence)." (SKILL.md) |
| R7 Code examples complete enough to run | ✅ yes | Complete theophylline example: "fit <- nlmixr2(one.compartment, theo_sd, est = \"saem\", saemControl(print = 0))" (SKILL.md) |
| R8 Examples run in continuous integration | ✅ yes | skill-examples.yaml: "Runs the fenced R code blocks shipped in inst/agents and inst/skills"; the estimation blocks are not in example_skips except two reference fragments. |
| R9 Continuous integration passes on the pinned commit | ✅ yes | skill-examples.yaml scheduled run on main at 50f236a (2026-10-26): success. |
| R10 Stores outputs from a real run | no | No stored outputs; the vitals evaluation writes to evals/logs/, which is git-ignored. |

- **❌ Major error.** "\| BSV% near 0 or > 100% \| ETA unsupported by data; remove it \|" (SKILL.md; repeated in references/model-building.md) Between-subject variability above 100% CV is common for absorption, lag time or bioavailability and is not evidence that the data fail to support the ETA; removing it pushes real variability into other parameters and the residual error (Savic and Karlsson 2009; Mould and Upton 2013).
- **❌ Major error.** "ETA shrinkage > ~30% means individual ETAs (and EBE-based diagnostics) are unreliable for that parameter; consider removing it or note the caveat." (references/model-building.md) Shrinkage measures how little the design says about each individual, not whether the population variance exists; it is a reason to distrust EBE-based diagnostics, not to remove the ETA (Savic and Karlsson 2009). The same class of error as known-answer fixture 1.

## nlmixr2lib · extract-literature-model {#nlmixr2lib-extract}

[nlmixr2/nlmixr2lib at `fcfe7a8`](https://github.com/nlmixr2/nlmixr2lib/tree/fcfe7a8d18a312b8797ce2e493fc83f68a6c0c80/.claude/skills/extract-literature-model) · tool skill · unproven: no evidence of use, so not ranked · tags: nlmixr2; model building from literature

| S | Q | E | M | U |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 21.9 | 0 | 48.0 | 98.9 | 0.0 |

**Quality.** 6 of 7 applicable rubric items met (85.7), less 4 major and 6 minor errors.

| Item | | Evidence |
|:---|:---|:---|
| R1 States what the skill does not do | ✅ yes | "This skill **only adds** new models. Retrofitting existing vignettes ... is a future separate skill." (SKILL.md) |
| R2 Cites sources for its recommendations | no | 4 of 10 sampled recommendations name a source (air docs, WHO weight-for-age curves, nlmixr2libingest, PKNCA vignette). |
| R6 States the limitations of its own output | ✅ yes | "**Assumptions and deviations** — explicit list of what you had to assume because the paper didn't say" (SKILL.md) |
| R7 Code examples complete enough to run | ✅ yes | Full render gate: "timeout 300 Rscript --vanilla -e \"pkgload::load_all(...); rmarkdown::render(...)\"" (SKILL.md) |
| R8 Examples run in continuous integration | ✅ yes | pkgdown.yaml "run: Rscript .github/scripts/pkgdown-parallel-build.R" renders every article the skill produces; R-CMD-check runs the model tests. |
| R9 Continuous integration passes on the pinned commit | ✅ yes | pkgdown.yaml run on main at fcfe7a8 (2026-10-24): success. |
| R10 Stores outputs from a real run | ✅ yes | The repository holds the models and rendered validation vignettes the workflow produced (inst/modeldb, vignettes/articles, gh-pages). |

- **❌ Major error.** "\| `Y = LOG(F) + EPS(1)` (log-transform-both-sides) \| `Cc ~ prop(propSd)` (NONMEM \"additive on log scale\" ≡ proportional in linear space)" (references/nonmem-translation.md; repeated in SKILL.md and verification-checklist.md) Additive error on the log scale is a log-normal error model; proportional error matches it only approximately for small sigma, so the translation changes the likelihood and the simulated spread. lnorm() is the exact translation (nlmixr2 residual-error documentation).
- **❌ Major error.** "`S1 = V/1000` (or similar) is a NONMEM unit-rescaling shorthand: dose in mg, volume in L, concentration in mg/L is the canonical case." (references/nonmem-translation.md) With dose in mg and V in L, S1 = V/1000 gives predictions in ug/L (ng/mL), not mg/L; dropping S1 and declaring mg/L makes Cc 1000-fold smaller than the data (NONMEM Users Guide VI, scale parameters).
- **❌ Major error.** "`lktr` — log first-order transit rate constant (= n_transit / MTT for a chain of length n)." (references/parameter-names.md) In the transit-compartment model ktr = (n+1)/MTT; n/MTT shortens the absorption delay, most when n is small (Savic et al. 2007, J Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn 34:711).
- **❌ Major error.** "# Replicates Figure 4 of <Author Year>: VPC of Cc vs. time by dose group." (references/vignette-template.md) Cc from rxSolve carries no residual error, so its percentiles are too narrow to compare with a published VPC, and the spread check against the paper can give the wrong conclusion (Bergstrand et al. 2011).
- **Minor error.** "`expSd` (used with `~ lnorm(...)`; ... the SD applies on the exponentiated scale)" (references/parameter-names.md) In nlmixr2, lnorm(sd) puts the SD on the log scale.
- **Minor error.** "etalcl ~ 0.186   # ... = 0.186 (43.1% CV)" (SKILL.md) 43.1% is sqrt(0.186); under the skill's own omega^2 = log(CV^2+1) rule the CV is 45.2%.
- **Minor error.** "The `A(1) = ...` initialization in `$DES` translates to `<state>(0) <- ...`" (references/nonmem-translation.md) NONMEM sets initial amounts through A_0 in $PK; A(n) is read-only in $DES (NONMEM Users Guide VIII).
- **Minor error.** "The PKNCA formula **must include a treatment grouping variable** (`conc ~ time \| id/treatment`)" (SKILL.md) In PKNCA the term after "/" is the analyte, so this makes treatment an analyte; it also contradicts the skill's own pknca-recipes.md (PKNCA documentation).
- **Minor error.** "The trajectory should monotonically approach the reported baseline (assuming a single stable attractor ...)" (references/endogenous-validation.md) A stable attractor can be approached with overshoot or oscillation, as in Friberg-type models, so the check would flag a correct model.
- **Minor error.** "With large IIV on a non-linear response, the median of the transform sits above the transform of the median." (references/known-vignette-failure-patterns.md) The median is unchanged by a monotonic transform; a gap needs a non-monotonic response or several random effects, and its direction is not fixed.

- **❌ Major error.** "`nonmem` needs no licence, only the output file: point `--nonmem-table` at a `$TABLE` and it compares against NONMEM's own PRED or IPRED for one subject," (references/validation.md) A subject's PRED uses that subject's covariates and doses, and IPRED adds its post-hoc ETAs, while the Jinko solve uses the model defaults, so agreement or disagreement says little about the conversion (NONMEM Users Guide).
- **Minor error.** "A population is degenerate at the moment of dosing, so those rows are dropped" (references/reporting.md) After an IV bolus the concentration is Dose/V, which varies between patients.

- **❌ Major error.** "A1_val_batch[:, cl_index] = -cl                          # vary the CL entry" (SKILL.md) A1 entries are first-order rate constants, so the elimination entry must be -CL/V (and include any outflow); putting a clearance there treats CL as k with V = 1 (Gabrielsson and Weiner).
- **Minor error.** "dA1[cl_index, 0] = -1.0              # d(A1_val[cl_index]) / d(CL)" (SKILL.md) The derivative of -CL/V with respect to CL is -1/V, so the sensitivities are scaled wrongly unless V = 1.
- **Minor error.** "... indirect-response (turnover) models, or any DAE system. These are not" (SKILL.md) A turnover model with a linear drug effect is bilinear and fits the solver's form; only Emax or Imax drug functions fall outside it (Dayneka, Garg and Jusko 1993).
- **Minor error.** "A1 = csr_matrix([[-0.3, 0.1], [0.3, -0.1]])" (SKILL.md) Each column sums to zero, so the labelled two-compartment model has no elimination.
